catalog_scope.purpose: Internal possibility catalogs for generating realistic future raw Account Aggregator-style financial data for Aarav and Priya without inventing random merchants, counterparties, rails, or missing everyday scenarios.
catalog_scope.non_scheduling_rule: This artifact defines what can realistically happen. It must not decide what definitely occurs, create dated transactions, create a daily/monthly/year sequence, assign balances, or emit raw AA payload.

global_generation_guardrails: Catalog items are possibilities, not commitments.
Select later only when day context, location, mood, weekday/weekend, time budget, account posture, and upcoming obligations make the item plausible.
Most selected days and months must remain boring and repeatable rather than dramatic.
Known recurring obligations may have exact known amounts here; all other spends use ranges.
Do not create account balances, raw AA payloads, daily life, month plans, or year arcs in this artifact.
Respect full-visibility assumptions for persona-owned accounts from the account universes.
Cash is not an AA account. Only ATM withdrawals/deposits are visible later.
Card purchases post to card accounts first. Deposit accounts are impacted only when card bills are paid.
Pay-later purchases post to the Simpl account first. Deposit accounts are impacted only when repayments happen.
Self-transfers must be traceable across visible owned accounts and must not be treated as income or spending.
Friend/family transfers are ordinary external UPI/IMPS/NEFT flows without product-side labels.
Use raw narration hints only as narration texture; never include internal intent/category/stress labels in final raw AA data.

persona_monthly_selection_caps.global_rule: Category frequencies are upper bounds, not targets. Later month/day generators must not select the high end of every category in the same month.

recurring_vs_optional_selection_rule: Items with fixed known amounts and protected monthly cadence should be generated by the recurring obligation scheduler, not randomly selected by the day generator. Optional lifestyle catalog items require day context, location, time budget, and financial posture. The field recurrence_selection_type is the machine-readable source of truth: known_locked_recurring and known_recurring_but_persona_conditional may be handled by recurring schedulers; optional_recurring_candidate, optional_context_selected, rare_event_selected, and financial_lifecycle_selected require explicit year/month/day context before generation.
same_need_deduplication_rule: For a single underlying need, choose one merchant and one payment rail unless the day story explicitly supports split fulfillment, cancellation, refund, retry, or fallback. Do not generate BigBasket plus Zepto plus Blinkit for the same grocery need, Uber plus Ola for the same commute leg, flight plus train for the same travel leg, or 1mg plus PharmEasy for the same medicine refill unless explicitly justified.
coverage_is_not_a_goal_rule: A good generated year does not need to use every catalog section or item. Unused catalog items are expected. The catalog defines possibility, not coverage targets.

UPI.deposit_impact: immediate visible debit/credit on source/destination bank account
UPI.typical_use: peers, staff, small merchants, family, quick commerce, autos

CARD.deposit_impact: no immediate deposit debit; purchase appears in credit card account first; deposit impact occurs when card bill is paid
CARD.typical_use: online merchants, subscriptions, travel, larger retail, ride-hailing

NET_BANKING.deposit_impact: visible deposit debit/credit through bank transfer or biller payment
NET_BANKING.typical_use: rent, investments, loan prepayments, taxes, insurance

AUTO_DEBIT.deposit_impact: visible scheduled debit on source account or credit card; must respect autopay/card rules
AUTO_DEBIT.typical_use: EMI, SIPs, RD, NPS, subscriptions, bills

BNPL.deposit_impact: purchase appears in Simpl pay-later account first; deposit impact occurs only when repayment is made from visible deposit account

CASH_ATM_VISIBLE_ONLY.deposit_impact: only ATM withdrawal/deposit visible; downstream cash merchant spends are not AA-visible
CASH_ATM_VISIBLE_ONLY.typical_use: cash-only shops, auto, mechanic, tiny purchases

IMPS.deposit_impact: immediate visible debit or credit on the source or destination bank account
IMPS.typical_use: family transfers, friend transfers, rent, urgent bank transfers, reimbursements, and larger peer/institution transfers

NEFT.deposit_impact: visible bank debit or credit, usually used for scheduled or formal bank transfers
NEFT.typical_use: rent, salary/reimbursement credits, loan prepayments, insurance/tax/institution transfers, and larger family transfers

aarav: Prefer card for online/lifestyle/travel/gadgets and UPI for peers, staff, family, small merchants.
Allow Simpl only during final 8 days before salary and only for food/quick commerce categories.
Financially chaotic but survivable: high outstanding and occasional partial/revolved card payment may happen later, but not every month.
Smoking/cigarette-related UPI/cash patterns are allowed, but do not make every day a visible smoke transaction.
Group fronting should produce gross merchant debit and later partial friend credits, often delayed or split.
Aarav can delay settlements and defer SIP in allowed months, but should not look insolvent every month.
Do not collect Rohan rent; only household split settlements with Rohan are valid.
Use scooter for ordinary mobility; cabs/autos rise with rain, alcohol, late work, or vehicle issues.
priya: Protect rent, family support, education loan EMI, staff payments, card full autopay, SIPs/RD/NPS before discretionary spends.
Do not use BNPL, do not revolve credit card balances, do not take cash advances, and do not routinely convert purchases into EMI.
Discretionary spend exists but is controlled: personal care, books, gifts, food, dating/social, and travel home within monthly ranges.
Stress should come from obligations: family medical, insurance premium, household repair, tax/investment pressure, or Kochi travel.
Allow realistic leaks and fatigue spends, especially after late work, but not impulsive debt behavior.
Use HDFC salary account as main obligation source; use ICICI buffer/RD/liquid fund only with visible transfer or redemption logic.
Cabs/metro/autos are plausible for Bellandur commute; Activa is for local errands only.
Kochi family support is regular; Ananya support is occasional and not monthly by default.
cross_persona_rules: Only select catalog items when later day context, location, weekday/weekend, mood, account posture, and obligations make them plausible.
Prefer boring repeatable life over dramatic events. Most months should not include rare/high-cost categories.
No final AA payload may contain internal labels, persona labels, category tags, stress tags, or explanations.

anti_overuse_rules: Do not select a merchant just because it exists in this catalog.
Do not stack multiple high-cost events in the same day unless the day context supports it.
Do not create travel, insurance, gadget purchase, medical event, and tax top-up in the same month unless the year arc explicitly marks it as a stress month.
Do not make Priya use BNPL or revolve her credit card.
Do not make Aarav pay every friend settlement perfectly on time.
Do not make every Friday a pub night.
Do not make every WFH day food-delivery-heavy.
Do not duplicate card purchases as bank debits.
Do not duplicate pay-later purchases as bank debits.
Do not treat self-transfers as income or spending.
Do not treat friend reimbursements as income unless product analysis later chooses to infer it with uncertainty.
Do not turn cash spends into AA-visible merchant transactions; only ATM withdrawals/deposits are visible.
Do not create large unexplained credits as rescue inflows.
Do not make all active months stressful or all stress months catastrophic.
Do not use the same delivery/quick-commerce merchant repeatedly when alternatives and context imply variety.
Do not give Priya Aarav-like chaotic pub, BNPL, cigarette, or revolving-card behavior.
Do not make Aarav perfectly disciplined for all obligations; allow survivable imperfections where later cashflow supports them.
Do not generate hospital payments or insurance reimbursements without a selected medical context.
Do not generate travel destination spends without travel booking/departure context.
Do not use internal category names or notes in the final raw AA output.
subscription_selection_rule: Generic subscription catalog items are candidates, not obligations. A later Subscription Lock or Month Plan must select exact active subscriptions, billing rails, billing cadence, and amounts before they become recurring generated transactions. Do not generate every subscription category just because it exists in this catalog.

recurrence_selection_type_definitions.known_locked_recurring: Known obligation or autopay that should appear on its cadence unless a later explicit failure/stress rule says otherwise.
recurrence_selection_type_definitions.known_recurring_but_persona_conditional: Known scheduled item whose occurrence depends on persona cashflow or context, such as Aarav SIP success/skip or variable household utility timing.
recurrence_selection_type_definitions.optional_recurring_candidate: Possible recurring subscription/service. Must not be generated until a later stage selects the exact active service and billing cadence.
recurrence_selection_type_definitions.optional_context_selected: Normal variable spend that requires day context, location, mood, balance posture, and time budget.
recurrence_selection_type_definitions.rare_event_selected: Rare, high-effort, event-led, or high-cost item that requires explicit year/month/day selection and should respect cooldowns.
recurrence_selection_type_definitions.financial_lifecycle_selected: Investment, redemption, loan, insurance, tax, reimbursement, refund, or policy lifecycle event that requires financial context and traceability.
